findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reader thread is never joined before the assertion runs, so deletedAll.set(true) can race past the reader loop and the test can pass without ever exercising concurrent access. CI gets a flaky/ineffective regression test: the NPE this PR fixes can reappear while the test stays green, because caughtExceptions is asserted while the reader thread may still be mid-request or may not have started before deletedAll flips to true. Fix requires joining the thread (with the loop also bounded so it terminates when the thread is slow) before assertThat.

[ADVISORY] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() yields null, changing the null-contract of a method callers may unbox to long. Any caller that assigns the result to a primitive long (Long unboxing) throws a NullPointerException at the call site instead of the original NPE inside getGroupModel(), so the PR may just relocate the crash rather than fix it; the deleted groups are removed underneath the cache, making this path reachable exactly in the concurrent-delete scenario the PR targets.

[BUG] Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() converts the cached-adapter NPE into a silent null contract violation that will NPE at unboxing sites. Any caller treating the result as a primitive long (e.g., admin console/REST count endpoints that unbox the Long) now throws a NullPointerException downstream instead of getting a stale-but-valid count; the fix trades a server-side cache race for a client-visible NPE with no error semantics.

[BUG] The fix patches only getSubGroupsCount while every sibling method on the same adapter (getSubGroupsStream, getName, getAttributes etc.) still calls getGroupModel(), which returns the same null model when the cached group was concurrently invalidated. The added test reads group briefs (which exercise getSubGroupsStream/search paths) concurrently with deletes; the same race produces NPE from those sibling methods, so the PR's own test can still fail intermittently — the root cause (null-returning modelSupplier during invalidation) is unhandled except at one call site.

[BUG] The reader thread is never joined and exceptions raised after deletedAll.set(true) are lost, so the assertion can pass even when the race it claims to cover actually fires. The test is flaky-by-design: the background thread keeps looping only until the flag flips, an exception thrown in the final iteration (or during the in-flight request) is recorded after assertThat runs, so a genuine regression in this exact fix passes CI — missing verification for the bug being fixed.

[ADVISORY] The new test never calls the subGroupsCount endpoint, so the single line of production logic changed in this PR (getSubGroupsCount null path) has no coverage. A regression in the null-return branch (e.g., reverting to getGroupModel() or returning a wrong value) goes undetected; the test exercises list/brief endpoints, not the count endpoint the fix targets.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the underlying group has been evicted/deleted, silently violating the method's contract instead of fixing the NPE. Callers of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount (e.g., admin console subgroup counts, GroupResource counts) unbox or compare the returned Long; a null return surfaces as an NPE or a wrong count at a different site than before, so the race is not actually prevented — it is relocated.

[ADVISORY] Only getSubGroupsCount was hardened against a null modelSupplier; every other method on GroupAdapter that dereferences the lazily-loaded model (getSubGroupsStream, getAttributes, getRoleMappingsStream, etc.) still races the same concurrent-delete path. The stated intent — prevent NPE on concurrent group access — is only enforced for one method; any admin or token issuance flow touching another accessor during group deletion still hits the original NPE.

[BUG] The reader thread is never joined and no barrier guarantees it starts before deletions begin, so createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti does not reliably exercise the concurrent read/delete race it was written to reproduce. The test passes vacuously (thread starts after all deletions) or asserts on caughtExceptions before the in-flight request has failed, producing a flaky test that provides no regression protection for the fix.

[ADVISORY] fail() is called inside the IntStream lambda but the loop continues creating groups and the test does not abort on first failure, mixing assertion semantics with partial setup. A later contributor debugging this test sees a confusing mix of created and failed groups; failure attribution is per-group rather than per-test, making diagnosis of CI failures harder.

[ADVISORY] The PR title claims a concurrency fix, but it also carries an unrelated behavioral change: deleting the private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement (plus its @Override addition on CachedGroup.getRealm), work not traceable to the stated intent. If the helper was dead code the deletion is safe, but bundling it into a concurrency-fix PR means a bisect landing on this commit misattributes any search-related regression to the NPE fix; reviewers of the stated scope were not asked to validate the removal.

[BUG] Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() replaces the NPE with a null Long that downstream callers unbox or aggregate, so the same race now surfaces as an NPE elsewhere (e.g. in the resource provider summing counts) instead of being handled as a retry/re-fetch. When a group is deleted concurrently, callers that do `long count = adapter.getSubGroupsCount()` or `mapToLong` on the stream get a NullPointerException at a site further from the cause; the contract of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is a non-null Long, and this diff silently widens it to nullable for only this one implementer while every other implementer still returns non-null, so callers cannot defensively code for it.

[ADVISORY] Only getSubGroupsCount() is patched with the null-guard; every other method on GroupAdapter that delegates through getGroupModel() (getSubGroupsStream, getAttributesStream, getRoleMappingsStream, etc.) still dereferences the invalidated model and NPEs under the identical concurrent-delete race. The race the PR claims to fix (concurrent group access NPE) remains reachable via any other read path on the adapter; the next reader hitting e.g. getSubGroupsStream during a delete gets the same 500, so the fix is one-method-wide where the defect is adapter-wide.

[BUG] The 'reader' thread calls groups(null, 0, MAX_VALUE, true) with brief=true, which excludes subGroupCount from the representation, so the test never exercises the changed getSubGroupsCount() code path — it is a stand-in guard that goes green while the patched code is never executed. The regression the PR fixes can be reintroduced and this test still passes, because the brief listing never calls into GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(); the concurrency race can recur in production while CI stays green.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is never joined and the assertion runs immediately after deletedAll.set(true), so exceptions thrown after the assertThat line are lost and the test can pass while the reader thread is mid-request that would have failed. Flaky false-green: on a machine where the delete loop finishes before the reader's in-flight request completes, a genuine NPE surfaces after the assertion and the test reports success; the guard does not actually observe the full read window it claims to cover.

[ADVISORY] Adding @Override to getRealm() implies a change in an interface/supertype contract (the method now overrides something new), and no corresponding change to that interface or its other implementers appears in this diff — if the interface method was added or its signature changed, out-of-tree implementers of the cached-entity contract silently stop overriding it and drift from the new contract. Custom/experimental implementations of the cache-entity interface (e.g. alternate cache stores in downstream forks) compile unchanged but no longer satisfy the new contract, and a rename or signature change in the parent becomes a silent behavioral break rather than a compile error.

[BUG] The fix changes getSubGroupsCount's contract to return null when the cached model is invalidated, which replaces the original NPE in this adapter with NPEs at every caller that unboxes or dereferences the returned Long. Any caller doing `long count = adapter.getSubGroupsCount()` or arithmetic/comparison on the result now throws NullPointerException at the call site instead of inside the cache adapter — the PR's stated intent (eliminate the NPE under concurrent delete) is not achieved, the failure is merely relocated, and a nullable Long in the admin API path can surface as a 500 or a JSON 'null' count breaking client deserialization.

[BUG] The regression test can pass vacuously because the reader thread races against `deletedAll.set(true)` and is never joined, so zero read iterations may occur before the deletes finish. The thread is started and `deletedAll` is set immediately after the sequential delete loop; the JVM may run the reader loop zero times (or the thread may be still starting), so the assertion on caughtExceptions validates nothing and a regression of the original NPE would go undetected in CI — the test does not preserve the PR's intent of proving the concurrent NPE is fixed.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement, an unrelated dead-code removal bundled into a PR whose accepted intent is 'fix concurrent group access NPE', silently widening the change's scope without explicit acceptance. Anyone bisecting a behavior change in group search or reviewing the NPE fix for backport must now reason about an orthogonal deletion in the same commit; if the method was actually referenced (or planned to be) by a search path, its removal changes filtering semantics with no test in this diff covering it.

[BUG] The new concurrency test asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader thread, so the assertion races the reader and passes even when the reader later throws. deletedAll.set(true) is set and assertThat runs immediately on the main thread while the reader thread may still be mid-request or not yet have recorded an exception; a test run where the reader thread throws after the assert has already executed reports green, so the exact NPE the PR claims to fix can still occur without failing this test — the test provides false confidence that the fix works.

[BUG] The reader thread's only synchronization with the deletes is the deletedAll flag checked before each read, so nothing guarantees any read overlaps the delete loop — the test can pass while never exercising the concurrent-delete/read path it claims to cover. The while loop checks deletedAll at the top and may run zero or few iterations before all deletes complete (thread start latency vs 100 sequential HTTP deletes is arbitrary); a run where the reader performs no reads during deletion passes trivially, and a run where reads do overlap may or may not hit the race — the test is a probabilistic race harness, not a verification of the fix, and will flake in both directions (false passes and potentially false failures from unrelated HTTP errors).

[BUG] The test never inspects the result of the read operation, only whether it throws — a tautological existence check on a call whose payload is discarded. managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) returns a GroupRepresentation list whose contents are thrown away; even if the fix produced wrong data (e.g., getSubGroupsCount() returning null propagating as a 0/missing subGroupCount in the brief representation), the test passes because no assertion checks the returned groups, count, or shape — the returned value of the fixed method is never verified anywhere in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new null-guard branch (model == null returning null) in getSubGroupsCount has no test that triggers it — the only new test exercises the admin REST path probabilistically and asserts nothing about the method's null return. Checked GroupTest.java in this diff (the sole test file modified): it asserts only that no exception is thrown at the HTTP layer; it never constructs or observes a GroupAdapter whose modelSupplier returns null, so the new branch's contract — returning null instead of NPE — is unverified, and a regression where the branch returns the wrong sentinel (e.g., 0L, changing semantics from 'unknown' to 'empty') would not be caught by anything in this diff; callers of getSubGroupsCount receiving null (e.g., representations building counts) also have no test confirming they tolerate it.

[ADVISORY] Creation failures inside the IntStream lambda call fail() inside a lambda, which throws from the lambda's thread-of-execution but here it's the test thread — however the collected groupUuuids list can be partially populated before failure, leaking the already-created groups into the realm for subsequent tests. If a create fails mid-loop, fail() aborts the test but the up-to-99 groups already created via managedRealm.admin() are never cleaned up (no @Cleanup/afterEach removal of groupUuuids), polluting the shared realm for other tests in the class and producing cascading unrelated failures in CI.

[ADVISORY] The NPE fix converts a crash into a silent null return from getSubGroupsCount, which callers that unbox the Long will turn back into an NPE at an unrelated site. When a group is deleted concurrently and the cached model's supplier yields null, getSubGroupsCount() returns null; any caller doing arithmetic or unboxing on the result (e.g. count comparisons in admin/REST count endpoints) throws NullPointerException far from the root cause, misdirecting debugging — the failure is neither observable at its origin nor honestly reported, and serialization of a null subGroupCount silently omits the field instead of erroring.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is never joined, so the test can assert and pass before the final read request finishes, and an exception thrown after deletedAll.set(true) is silently dropped. The test asserts caughtExceptions is empty at the moment deletedAll is set, while the reader thread may still be mid-request or throw afterwards; a race-reproducing failure occurs after the assertion and is never recorded, so the test reports success while dropping the very failure it exists to catch.
